questions_and_answers.question: Suppose a bank makes a loan to a small business so that the business can purchase a new machine press. Which of the following are true of that event? A. The bank becomes more liquid. B. The business becomes more liquid. C. The business takes on a liability in the form of the loan agreement (the business' promise to repay the loan). D. The bank holds an asset in the form of the checking account opened up for the business. E. The bank holds an asset in the form of the loan agreement (the business' promise to repay the loan).
questions_and_answers.answer: The business takes on a liability in the form of the loan agreement (the business' promise to repay the loan) The bank holds an asset in the form of the loan agreement (the business' promise to repay the loan) The bank holds an asset in the form of the checking account opened up for the business. When a bank lends money to a small business , it creates a liability for the business. The business is obligated to repay the loan according to the terms of the loan agreement. This liability is recorded on the balance sheet of the business as a debt or a payable. Therefore, the statement "The business takes on a liability in the form of the loan agreement" is true. On the other hand, for the bank, the loan agreement represents an asset. The bank has the legal right to receive the principal amount and the interest payments from the business.
